requirement.evidence: Under a no-fault just cause termination, the owner shall either provide 3 months of relocation assistance or waive payment of rent for the final 3 months of the tenancy.
requirement.note: The 30 days, written notice, cure period, and no-fault causes are all in the document. The card's phrase "for at-fault causes must first give you a chance to fix" is a slight narrowing: the document says notice of violation with time to fix comes before a just cause termination notice. The "3 months" relocation or waiver is stated.

coverage.evidence: The Just Cause Ordinance shall not apply to certain types of residential property, including housing produced in the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable housing; hotel and transient occupancy; hospital and care facilities; dormitories; and other shared living quarters.
coverage.note: The 15-year exemption is stated. The card omits the other exemptions (deed-restricted housing, hotels, and so on). Also, the document gives no cutoff date for the 15 years.

citation.evidence: The Santa Ana City Council on Tuesday night adopted two new ordinances to help protect renters: a Rent Stabilization Ordinance, which limits residential rent increases to no more than 3% per year, and a Just Cause Eviction Ordinance, which limits the allowed reasons for which a renter can be evicted.
citation.note: The ordinance is named in the document, but no section number is given.

requirement.evidence: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period. If the CPI is negative, no rent increase is permitted.
requirement.note: The cap, CPI rule, June 30 publication, September 1 effective date, and notice requirement are all supported. The building-date scope is "constructed after February 1, 1995" exempt, so the card's "on or before" is a reasonable inverse. The mobile home space exemption is omitted.
